# Spec-feature coverage matrix (M5 WP7, )

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/samples/spec_feature_matrix.py --write. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Every spec **feature** is a kernel-primitive requirement carried in a spec's
`targetRequirements`. Target profiles match primitives, not domain labels (),
so this matrix is keyed by the closed primitive glue vocabulary (the union of
`supportedFeatures` and `unsupportedConstructs` across the committed target
profiles). A feature outside that vocabulary is an unglued term and fails the gate
before any renderer.

**Coverage denominator.** The denominator is the profile-*supported* primitive
vocabulary — not explicitly unsupported constructs and not every primitive the
kernel could theoretically emit. So this matrix proves a two-sided closure: every
profile-supported primitive is exercised by a fixture (coverage), and every feature
a spec emits is explicitly supported or unsupported (glue). It does **not** claim
"every kernel primitive is exercised": a primitive
the kernel could emit that no spec emits *and* no profile declares is dormant and
invisible to both sides by design.

## Feature -> fixtures / lowerings

The `lowerings on covering fixtures` column is **fixture-granularity**: the union
of committed backend lowerings across the fixtures that carry this feature — NOT a
claim that this specific feature is exercised through that lowering. Per-feature
lowering coverage is the lowering-level gate, tracked in .
